messages.text:
"🥊 TG BOXING – THE GLORY OF CHAMPIONS

CRIE UM JOGO DE BOXE 3D COMPLETO, PROFISSIONAL E MULTIPLAYER

Desenvolva um jogo de boxe 3D extremamente completo, com gráficos bonitos, animações fluidas, personagens totalmente personalizáveis, modo carreira, campeonatos mundiais, cinturões, rankings, sistema de nocautes, notícias dinâmicas e multiplayer online.

O jogo deve ter identidade própria, com uma apresentação inspirada na intensidade dos animes de boxe, especialmente na energia das lutas de Hajime no Ippo, mas com personagens, cenários, movimentos, animações e identidade visual originais.

O nome oficial será TG BOXING – THE GLORY OF CHAMPIONS.

A experiência deve parecer um verdadeiro simulador de carreira de boxe, com elementos de arcade, proporcionando lutas emocionantes e competitivas.

---

1. GRÁFICOS E APRESENTAÇÃO 3D

Crie um mundo totalmente tridimensional.

REQUISITOS:

- Personagens 3D detalhados.
- Modelos corporais personalizáveis.
- Animações fluidas e naturais.
- Expressões faciais durante as lutas.
- Suor e efeitos visuais de impacto moderados.
- Iluminação dinâmica nas arenas.
- Público com animações próprias.
- Árbitros e treinadores.
- Câmeras cinematográficas.
- Replays dos melhores momentos.
- Animações de entrada dos lutadores.
- Animações de vitória e derrota.
- Interface moderna e profissional.

As lutas precisam ter movimentos rápidos, esquivas, movimentação lateral, aproximação, afastamento e movimentação de cabeça.

A câmera deve lembrar jogos profissionais de boxe, mostrando os dois lutadores de maneira clara.

Criar também uma câmera cinematográfica para nocautes e momentos especiais.

2. CRIAÇÃO DE LUTADOR – PERSONALIZAÇÃO EXTREMA

O jogador poderá criar seu próprio boxeador do zero.

Quero pelo menos 100 opções de personalização por categoria, quando aplicável.

CABELO:

- 100 cortes diferentes.
- Cabelos curtos, longos, raspados e estilos diferentes.
- Cores naturais e fantasia.
- Barbas e bigodes.
- Sobrancelhas personalizadas.

ROSTO:

- Diferentes formatos de rosto.
- Olhos, nariz e boca personalizáveis.
- Tons de pele variados.
- Marcas e detalhes faciais.
- Cicatrizes cosméticas.
- Expressões faciais.

CORPO:

- Altura configurável.
- Envergadura configurável.
- Diferentes estruturas corporais.
- Lutadores musculosos, magros, pesados e robustos.
- Personalização das proporções corporais dentro de limites equilibrados.

ROUPAS:

- Pelo menos 100 opções de shorts.
- 100 opções de camisetas e regatas.
- 100 opções de calçados.
- 100 opções de roupões de entrada.
- 100 combinações de cores.
- Uniformes especiais de campeonato.

LUVAS:

- 100 modelos de luvas.
- Diferentes formatos e estilos.
- Cores personalizáveis.
- Luvas clássicas, modernas e especiais.
- Possibilidade de criar combinações próprias.

ACESSÓRIOS:

- Bandagens.
- Protetores de cabeça para treinos.
- Chuteiras não são necessárias: utilizar calçados próprios de boxe.
- Medalhas e acessórios cosméticos.
- Personalização de nome e apelido.

Criar um editor visual com pré-visualização 3D em tempo real.

3. SISTEMA DE MOVIMENTAÇÃO E COMBATE

O combate deve ser o coração do jogo.

Criar um sistema de luta com animações originais, inspiradas na intensidade e fluidez dos animes de boxe.

MOVIMENTOS:

- Jab.
- Direto.
- Cruzado.
- Gancho.
- Uppercut.
- Esquivas.
- Bloqueios.
- Passos laterais.
- Movimentação para frente e para trás.
- Combinações de golpes.
- Contra-ataques.
- Recuperação de equilíbrio.
- Movimentos defensivos.
- Animações de cansaço.

Criar animações diferentes para cada tipo de lutador.

Um lutador pesado deve apresentar movimentação diferente de um lutador mais leve.

Criar estilos de boxe com características próprias:

- Agressivo.
- Defensivo.
- Técnico.
- Contra-atacador.
- Velocista.
- Lutador de pressão.

O combate precisa considerar:

- Resistência.
- Energia.
- Precisão.
- Velocidade.
- Defesa.
- Potência.
- Recuperação.
- Condicionamento.

Não permitir que o jogador fique atacando infinitamente sem consequências. O gerenciamento de energia deve ser importante.

4. SISTEMA DE NOCAUTE

Criar um sistema de nocautes dinâmico.

Possibilidades:

- Nocaute técnico.
- Nocaute por contagem.
- Vitória por decisão dos juízes.
- Vitória por interrupção do árbitro.
- Empate.
- Abandono da luta.

Criar animações cinematográficas para momentos decisivos.

Após um nocaute:

- A luta é interrompida.
- O árbitro inicia a contagem.
- O resultado aparece na tela.
- A torcida reage.
- O narrador anuncia o vencedor.
- O histórico registra o resultado.

Adicionar sistema de replay com câmera lenta.

5. MODO CARREIRA – SEJA UMA LENDA

Este será um dos principais modos do jogo.

O jogador começa como um boxeador desconhecido, com poucos recursos e sem títulos.

Ele precisará construir sua reputação até chegar ao topo do boxe mundial.

FUNCIONALIDADES:

- Criar o próprio lutador.
- Escolher nome e apelido.
- Escolher nacionalidade.
- Começar em pequenas competições.
- Assinar contratos.
- Receber propostas de luta.
- Negociar premiações.
- Ganhar dinheiro.
- Comprar equipamentos.
- Treinar atributos.
- Melhorar habilidades.
- Participar de campeonatos.
- Conquistar cinturões.
- Defender títulos.
- Tornar-se campeão mundial.
- Enfrentar antigos rivais.
- Construir uma carreira histórica.

Cada luta deve alterar a trajetória do personagem.

Criar um calendário de carreira com datas, eventos e próximas lutas.

Adicionar um sistema de reputação que influencia os adversários e as propostas recebidas.

6. SISTEMA DE ADVERSÁRIOS E NPCs

Criar pelo menos 100 lutadores NPC diferentes.

Cada um deve ter:

- Nome.
- Sobrenome.
- Apelido.
- Nacionalidade.
- Idade fictícia.
- Peso.
- Altura.
- Envergadura.
- Estilo de luta.
- Personalidade.
- Atributos.
- Histórico.
- Vitórias.
- Derrotas.
- Empates.
- Vitórias por nocaute.

Criar lutadores invictos, veteranos, jovens promessas, campeões e antigos campeões.

Exemplo de lutadores:

- Diego \"The Beast\" Moreira – 22 vitórias, 0 derrotas.
- Marcus \"Iron Fist\" Carter – 31 vitórias, 4 derrotas.
- Kenji \"The Storm\" Takahashi – 18 vitórias, 1 derrota.
- Rafael \"El Toro\" Santos – 26 vitórias, 3 derrotas.
- Victor \"Nightmare\" Williams – 40 vitórias, 2 derrotas.

Os nomes são exemplos. Criar um elenco muito maior.

Os NPCs precisam ter inteligência artificial para:

- Atacar.
- Defender.
- Recuar.
- Procurar oportunidades.
- Administrar energia.
- Mudar de comportamento durante a luta.
- Reagir à situação do combate.

Os adversários devem possuir níveis de dificuldade diferentes.

7. SISTEMA PROFISSIONAL DE BOXE E CINTURÕES

Criar uma estrutura completa de competições profissionais.

Adicionar as seguintes categorias de peso:

- Peso-mosca.
- Peso-galo.
- Peso-pena.
- Peso-leve.
- Peso-superleve.
- Peso-meio-médio.
- Peso-médio.
- Peso-supermédio.
- Peso-meio-pesado.
- Peso-cruzador.
- Peso-pesado.

Criar organizações e federações fictícias inspiradas nas grandes organizações do boxe profissional.

Cada federação terá:

- Ranking próprio.
- Campeão atual.
- Cinturão.
- Desafiantes.
- Eliminatórias.
- Defesas obrigatórias.
- Eventos especiais.

Criar cinturões com modelos 3D detalhados.

Adicionar:

- Cinturão nacional.
- Cinturão continental.
- Cinturão internacional.
- Cinturão mundial.
- Cinturão interino.
- Cinturão de campeão absoluto.
- Cinturão de campeão dos campeões.

O jogador poderá conquistar cinturões em diferentes categorias de peso, respeitando as regras da carreira.

Criar animações de entrega de cinturão e comemoração.

8. RANKINGS E CLASSIFICAÇÕES

Criar rankings mundiais atualizados automaticamente.

Cada categoria terá:

- TOP 100 lutadores.
- Campeão.
- Desafiante número 1.
- Desafiantes.
- Lutadores em ascensão.
- Lutadores em decadência.

O ranking deve mudar de acordo com os resultados.

Vencer um adversário bem colocado deve proporcionar maior evolução na classificação.

Perder pode fazer o lutador cair no ranking.

Criar uma tela de estatísticas com:

- Mais vitórias.
- Mais nocautes.
- Maior sequência invicta.
- Mais defesas de cinturão.
- Campeão mais dominante.
- Lutador do ano.
- Revelação do ano.

9. MULTIPLAYER ONLINE – DESAFIE SEUS AMIGOS

Este sistema é obrigatório e precisa funcionar de verdade.

Quero poder criar uma sala de luta e compartilhar um LINK com outra pessoa.

Funcionamento:

1. O jogador entra no multiplayer.
2. Clica em CRIAR SALA.
3. O jogo cria uma sala online.
4. Gera um link exclusivo de convite.
5. O jogador copia e envia o link pelo WhatsApp ou outra plataforma.
6. O amigo abre o link.
7. Entra na sala.
8. Os dois escolhem seus lutadores.
9. Começa a luta online.

Criar:

- Salas privadas.
- Salas públicas.
- Convites por link.
- Código de sala.
- Sistema de reconexão.
- Sincronização dos jogadores.
- Sincronização de movimentação.
- Sincronização dos golpes.
- Sincronização de placar.
- Sistema contra desconexões.
- Histórico de confrontos.

IMPORTANTE: implementar multiplayer com comunicação em tempo real usando backend e WebSocket ou tecnologia equivalente.

Não simular multiplayer com dois personagens controlados localmente.

Os dois jogadores precisam conseguir jogar de dispositivos diferentes.

10. TG COIN – ECONOMIA DO JOGO

Criar uma moeda oficial chamada TG COIN.

Ela será utilizada para:

- Comprar roupas.
- Comprar luvas.
- Comprar equipamentos.
- Desbloquear cosméticos.
- Comprar roupões.
- Personalizar personagens.
- Comprar itens de treinamento.
- Participar de eventos especiais.

O jogador poderá ganhar TG COIN através de:

- Vitórias.
- Campeonatos.
- Missões.
- Conquistas.
- Contratos.
- Premiações.
- Eventos especiais.

APOSTAS ENTRE JOGADORES:

Adicionar um sistema opcional de desafios amistosos em que dois jogadores colocam uma quantidade de TG COIN em disputa, dentro de limites definidos pelo jogo.

O vencedor recebe a recompensa conforme as regras da partida.

Criar proteção contra duplicação de moedas, manipulação de resultados e fraudes.

A economia deve ser inteiramente virtual, sem dinheiro real.

11. ITENS DE TREINAMENTO E EVOLUÇÃO

Criar uma loja com itens fictícios de evolução e treinamento.

Adicionar:

- Equipamentos de academia.
- Sacos de pancada.
- Luvas de treinamento.
- Acessórios.
- Itens cosméticos.
- Impulsionadores fictícios de treinamento.

Os impulsionadores devem ser itens inteiramente fictícios, sem representar substâncias reais ou incentivar seu uso.

Cada lutador possui atributos que evoluem de acordo com seu treinamento e desempenho.

ATRIBUTOS:

- Força.
- Velocidade.
- Resistência.
- Precisão.
- Defesa.
- Reflexos.
- Mobilidade.
- Recuperação.
- Condicionamento.

Criar um limite de evolução para manter o equilíbrio competitivo.

12. SISTEMA DE ACADEMIA E TREINAMENTO

O jogador poderá administrar sua preparação entre as lutas.

Criar uma academia 3D com:

- Sacos de pancada.
- Ringue de treinamento.
- Equipamentos.
- Treinadores.
- Outros boxeadores.
- Área de preparação.

Criar atividades de treinamento com pequenas interações.

O jogador poderá melhorar atributos, desenvolver seu estilo e preparar-se para o próximo adversário.

Adicionar um treinador que oferece comentários sobre o desempenho.

13. SISTEMA DE NOTÍCIAS DINÂMICAS

Criar um jornal esportivo dentro do jogo chamado TG BOXING NEWS.

Ele deverá produzir notícias automaticamente com base nos acontecimentos do universo do jogo.

Exemplos:

\"ÚLTIMA HORA: Diego Moreira mantém sua invencibilidade após vitória impressionante.\"

\"CAMPEONATO MUNDIAL: Rafael Santos conquista o cinturão dos pesos-médios.\"

\"REVIRAVOLTA: Ex-campeão perde sua posição no TOP 10 após nova derrota.\"

\"PROMESSA DO ANO: Jovem lutador conquista sua quinta vitória consecutiva.\"

\"GRANDE ANÚNCIO: Uma revanche histórica foi confirmada para o próximo sábado.\"

As notícias devem ser geradas usando dados reais do próprio jogo.

Criar categorias:

- Últimas notícias.
- Resultados.
- Transferências e contratos.
- Próximas lutas.
- Campeonatos.
- Rankings.
- Rivalidades.
- Recordes.
- Entrevistas.

Adicionar manchetes, imagens, datas e nomes dos envolvidos.

14. ENTREVISTAS E RIVALIDADES

Criar rivalidades entre lutadores.

Antes das lutas importantes:

- Entrevistas.
- Coletivas de imprensa.
- Provocações fictícias.
- Desafios públicos.
- Declarações dos treinadores.

Depois das lutas:

- Entrevistas com o vencedor.
- Comentários do derrotado.
- Reações dos fãs.
- Possibilidade de revanche.

As rivalidades devem influenciar a narrativa da carreira.

15. SISTEMA DE COMPETIÇÕES

Criar eventos de diferentes tamanhos.

- Campeonatos regionais.
- Campeonatos nacionais.
- Campeonatos continentais.
- Torneios internacionais.
- Eliminatórias mundiais.
- Grandes noites de boxe.
- Eventos especiais.
- Torneios de campeões.

Criar cartazes de eventos, card principal, lutas preliminares e luta principal.

Cada evento terá data, local, premiação e participantes.

16. ARENAS E RINGUES

Criar pelo menos 15 arenas diferentes.

Exemplos:

- Academia de bairro.
- Ginásio municipal.
- Arena nacional.
- Ginásio internacional.
- Grande estádio.
- Arena de campeonato mundial.
- Arena subterrânea fictícia.
- Ginásio japonês.
- Arena brasileira.
- Arena americana.

Cada ambiente deve possuir iluminação, decoração, público e identidade próprios.

Criar diferentes formatos de apresentação do ringue.

17. SISTEMA DE PREMIAÇÕES E RECORDES

Criar uma cerimônia de premiação anual.

Categorias:

- Lutador do ano.
- Nocaute do ano.
- Melhor luta do ano.
- Melhor revelação.
- Melhor campeão.
- Melhor sequência invicta.
- Melhor retorno.
- Melhor defesa de cinturão.
- Maior rivalidade.
- Melhor treinador.

As premiações devem considerar os resultados registrados no jogo.

Criar uma galeria de troféus e conquistas.

18. INTERFACE E MENUS

Criar uma interface bonita e moderna.

MENU PRINCIPAL:

- Modo carreira.
- Multiplayer.
- Criar lutador.
- Rankings.
- TG Boxing News.
- Loja.
- Academia.
- Estatísticas.
- Configurações.

O menu deve apresentar o lutador principal em um ambiente 3D.

Criar animações de transição e efeitos visuais discretos.

19. SALVAMENTO E SISTEMA DE DADOS

Implementar salvamento persistente.

Salvar:

- Personagem.
- Aparência.
- Atributos.
- Dinheiro.
- TG COIN.
- Vitórias.
- Derrotas.
- Empates.
- Nocautes.
- Cinturões.
- Ranking.
- Contratos.
- Notícias.
- Histórico de lutas.
- Progresso da carreira.

O multiplayer precisa utilizar dados sincronizados no servidor.

Não perder o progresso ao fechar ou atualizar o jogo.

20. QUALIDADE TÉCNICA E DESEMPENHO

O jogo precisa ser otimizado para dispositivos móveis.

Priorizar:

- 60 FPS como meta.
- Modelos 3D otimizados.
- Texturas eficientes.
- Iluminação otimizada.
- Animações leves.
- Carregamento progressivo.
- Interface responsiva.
- Controles touchscreen.
- Suporte a teclado e mouse quando disponível.

Criar controles virtuais para celulares:

- Joystick de movimentação.
- Botões de golpes.
- Botão de defesa.
- Botão de esquiva.
- Botão de movimentação especial.

Permitir personalização da posição e tamanho dos controles.

---

21. REGRAS FUNDAMENTAIS DE DESENVOLVIMENTO

NÃO CRIE APENAS UMA DEMONSTRAÇÃO VISUAL.

Quero um jogo realmente funcional.

Regras obrigatórias:

1. Todos os botões precisam funcionar.
2. Todos os menus precisam abrir corretamente.
3. O modo carreira precisa salvar e carregar dados.
4. As lutas precisam ter início, desenvolvimento e resultado.
5. Os NPCs precisam possuir inteligência artificial.
6. Os rankings precisam atualizar.
7. As notícias precisam refletir os acontecimentos reais.
8. Os cinturões precisam ser conquistáveis.
9. O multiplayer precisa permitir partidas reais entre dois dispositivos.
10. Os links de convite precisam funcionar.
11. As moedas precisam ter saldo persistente.
12. A personalização precisa funcionar visualmente.
13. As animações precisam estar conectadas às ações dos personagens.

Não colocar botões decorativos que não fazem nada.

Se algum sistema precisar de backend, implementar a estrutura necessária e explicar quais serviços precisam ser configurados.

Se não for possível implementar todos os sistemas de uma vez, construir por etapas, mantendo a arquitetura preparada para receber as próximas funcionalidades.

PRIORIDADE ABSOLUTA:

1. Sistema de combate 3D.
2. Movimentação e animações.
3. Criação e personalização de lutadores.
4. Modo carreira.
5. NPCs e inteligência artificial.
6. Sistema de cinturões e rankings.
7. Multiplayer por link.
8. TG COIN.
9. Notícias dinâmicas.
10. Academia, premiações e conteúdo adicional.

O resultado deve ser um verdadeiro universo de boxe, onde cada lutador possui uma história, cada vitória tem importância e cada cinturão representa uma conquista.

TG BOXING – THE GLORY OF CHAMPIONS.

A estrada para se tornar uma lenda começa no primeiro round.    Lutas cinematográficas
Animações fluidas, esquivas, contra-ataques e nocautes.
Campeonatos mundiais
Cinturões, defesas de título e rankings.
Personagens personalizados
Centenas de combinações de aparência e roupas.
Multiplayer online
Criar sala, compartilhar link e enfrentar amigos.

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

# 🤯 OMG — Oh My GitHub. ### 🚀 One Prompt In. A Full Game or App Out. 🚀 [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-🔥%20works-brightgreen?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/denaidark/OhMyGithub?style=for-the-badge&logo=github)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/issues) [![GitHub Actions](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub%20Actions-automated-2088FF?style=for-the-badge&logo=githubactions&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![OpenCode](https://img.shields.io/badge/powered%20by-OpenCode-111111?style=for-the-badge)](https://opencode.ai/) ```text ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗ ║ DESCRIBE IT → BUILD IT → TEST IT → PLAY IT ║ ║ ║ ║ One GitHub issue. One prompt. A complete project. ║ ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝ ``` **No API keys to configure. No server to maintain. No local setup maze.**
--- ## 🤯 What Is OMG? > **Your GitHub issue becomes the product brief.** OMG (Oh My GitHub) is an automated GitHub Actions workflow for creating complete browser games and app projects from one natural-language prompt. Write what you want in an issue and add the `OpenCode` label. OpenCode checks out the project, uses the shared skills, builds the experience, runs tests, verifies the result, and publishes an immutable OmGithub project link from the finished commit. Yes, it creates the code. Yes, it runs the verification loop. Yes, it can expose the result in a temporary browser URL. ## 🧠 TL;DR 1. Open a GitHub issue. 2. Describe the game or app you want. 3. Add the `OpenCode` label to the issue. 4. Let GitHub Actions build, test, verify, and propose the result. ```text Your idea → GitHub issue → OpenCode → tests → immutable OmGithub project ``` ## ⚡ Quick Start Create an issue in your repository with a concrete request: ```text Build a neon asteroid game. Requirements: - Arrow-key movement - Score and restart button - Win and lose states - Responsive browser layout - Run tests and verify it in a browser ``` That is the whole user-facing workflow. GitHub Actions handles the runner, OpenCode handles implementation, and the workflow handles verification plus the immutable project commit. To run against an existing non-default branch, end the issue title with a `branch: ` directive. The directive selects the checkout and is removed before the issue body is sent to OpenCode: ```sh gh issue create \ --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub \ --title "Custom branch smoke test branch: codex/omgithub-site" \ --body "Build a tiny browser page." \ --label Goal \ --label OpenCode ``` The GitHub App validates the branch before dispatching. If the directive is absent, the repository default branch remains the target. ## 🌍 What Can You Build? | 🎯 Use case | ✨ Example | |---|---| | 🎮 Arcade games | Breakout, Space Invaders, Asteroids, Match-3 | | 🧩 Puzzle games | Word games, logic puzzles, card games | | 🏃 Interactive demos | Physics experiments, simulations, visual toys | | 📊 Dashboards | Filters, charts, status panels, analytics views | | 🛠️ Internal tools | Trackers, generators, small workflow apps | | 🌐 Landing pages | Product pages, portfolios, interactive showcases | | 🧪 Prototypes | Turn a product idea into a runnable proof of concept | | 📱 Browser apps | Responsive tools that work on desktop and mobile | ## 🧰 What Happens Automatically? > **The workflow is the product.** - 📥 Checks out your repository and the shared OpenCode skills. - 🏷️ Synchronizes `model/*` and `skill/*` labels. - 🧭 Reads issue labels to select the model and requested skills. - 🤖 Runs OpenCode against the current project. - 🧪 Runs a second verification prompt after implementation. - 🌐 Starts the app and checks the local runtime. - 🔗 Creates a temporary public preview URL when verification passes. - 🔀 Creates and pushes an `opencode/` branch. - 🕹️ Adds an `Open Project` link backed by the repository path, with full-commit links retained for compatibility. - 💬 Posts progress and access details back to the issue. - 🧹 Cleans up temporary tunnels and runner processes. ## 🏷️ Model and Skill Labels Labels let you control the workflow without editing YAML. ```text model/opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free skill/load-sketchfab-threejs skill/gauntlet-loop ``` The workflow validates the selected labels, passes them into OpenCode, and records the resolved model and skills in the run logs. Shared skills are discovered from: ```text .agents/skills//SKILL.md ``` ## 🔄 OpenCode Workflow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Trigger] --> B[Prepare project] B --> C[Run build.md] C --> D[Run verify.md] D --> E{Public app works?} E -- No --> F[Run public-app-fix.md] F --> E E -- Yes --> G[Run completion-report.md] G --> H{Screenshots exist?} H -- No --> I[Run screenshot-evidence.md] I --> H H -- Yes --> J[Commit and push] J --> K[Create immutable project link] K --> L[Publish report] L --> M[Complete] ``` ## 🏗️ Architecture ```text ┌──────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ │ GitHub issue │ ──▶ │ GitHub Actions │ ──▶ │ OpenCode │ │ + issue text │ │ runner + labels │ │ + .agents │ └──────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ └──────┬───────┘ │ ┌─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┐ ▼ ▼ ▼ Build code Run tests Verify app │ │ │ └─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┘ ▼ ┌────────────────────────┐ │ Commit store + preview │ └────────────────────────┘ ``` ## 🔐 Security and Access - 🔑 You do not need to create or store a project-specific AI API key. - 🖥️ You do not need to operate a dedicated build server. - ☁️ Execution happens in GitHub Actions. - 🔒 Temporary SSH and preview access exists only for the workflow run. - 👀 Review the generated commit before integrating it. - 🛡️ Restrict who can apply the `OpenCode` label in repositories that accept public issues. > “No servers needed” means no servers for you to provision or maintain. The workflow still uses GitHub-hosted Actions infrastructure and temporary workflow services. ## 📁 Project Structure ```text 📦 OMG ├─ .github/workflows/opencode.yml # 🤖 Main issue-to-project workflow ├─ wiki/opencode.md # 📖 Workflow and session notes ├─ wiki/testing.md # 🧪 Verification guidance └─ AGENTS.md # 🧭 Repository instructions ``` ## 🧪 Local Validation Validate the workflow definition before pushing changes: ```sh actionlint .github/workflows/opencode.yml git diff --check ``` ## 🐛 Troubleshooting | Problem | What to check | |---|---| | The workflow did not start | Confirm the `OpenCode` label is applied to the issue. | | A skill was not selected | Add a matching `skill/` label. | | The app URL is missing | Check the local app verification step and runner log. | | The PR was not created | Confirm OpenCode produced a diff and the workflow reached the PR step. | | The workflow ran unexpectedly | Tighten the trigger condition and trusted-user policy. | ## 🤝 Contributing Ideas, skills, game templates, verification improvements, and workflow fixes are welcome. 1. Open an issue describing the improvement. 2. Add the `OpenCode` label when you want the workflow to prototype it. 3. Review the generated commit and Open Project page carefully. 4. Add tests and runtime proof for workflow changes. ## ⭐ The Pitch The old workflow was: idea → tickets → scaffolding → setup → implementation → debugging → deployment. The OMG workflow is: **idea → issue → playable project.** If you believe software should start with a sentence instead of a sprint plan, [⭐ star the repository](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub) and try it.
**Built with GitHub Actions, OpenCode, shared skills, and unreasonable optimism.** 😏

Keep the local [game issue E2E skill](.agents/skills/game-issue-e2e/SKILL.md) aligned with this workflow. Create an issue with `OpenCode` and only user-requested mode labels already attached, to start the native `issues.opened` listener. Wait only for the initial OpenCode session link during E2E kickoff. Install the listener on the default branch before requesting execution. Validate author access and freeze the request inside Actions before starting the reusable execution job. Set repository variable `OPENCODE_ACCESS=everyone` to accept any issue author for labeled issues. Keep the App as a setup helper. Use Actions concurrency to serialize each issue. Store `branch` in an `omgithub-request:v1` JSON HTML comment to select the project checkout, result base, and workflow. Let default-branch preparation dispatch the selected branch. Run preparation and OpenCode in that branch run. ## Shell timing When writing shell scripts, always add explicit per-command execution-time measurements between commands. Use `/usr/bin/time -p` or a small timing helper around each meaningful command; the outer command duration is not sufficient because it hides which step is slow or hung. Use `/usr/bin/time` only in scripts; do not invoke it directly in interactive shell commands. ## Ideas Store durable implementation ideas as individual Markdown files under `./ideas/`, using descriptive kebab-case filenames such as `ideas/opencode-oauth-env-auth.md`. ## Links in handoffs When a relevant URL or stable identifier exists, include a clickable Markdown link in the user-facing response. Link GitHub issues, Actions runs, pull requests, commits, releases, public app URLs, and Codex tasks/threads rather than reporting only their numbers or plain text. For Codex tasks/threads, use the `codex://threads/` URL format. When mentioning a commit, append its relative age in hours or days. ## OpenCode GitHub Actions To execute an issue, create it with `OpenCode` and only mode labels explicitly requested by the user. Check for a native `issues` run and successful preparation. The workflow starts a temporary AgentsWeb SSH session, verifies it, runs OpenCode, and cleans up the SSH session afterward. When monitoring a triggered run, use `gh run watch --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --exit-status` for overall job status. Do not use `gh run view --log` to read logs from a running task: GitHub reports that logs are unavailable until completion. Use `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh ` for the live Actions log over SSH. Do not use tight `for` loops around `gh run list`, which needlessly consume GitHub API rate limit. Free OpenCode models are limited per egress IP, not per account. Treat a local `FreeUsageLimitError` 429 as local only. Read the runner's own `Selected model` and provider errors before blaming quota. Use `retryAfterMs` as the reset bound. Run repeated V2 tests with a connected provider; do not spend the free allowance on retries. Interrupting a V2 turn before the assistant message projects leaves no stopped message to save. Wait for that assistant message before requiring the interrupted idle marker. To connect to an issue's live worker, find its run ID with `gh run list --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --workflow opencode.yml --status in_progress`, then run `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh ` to discover the host and port and SSH with `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb` as shown by the helper. The runner uploads chunks from `_diag/blocks` to GitHub. Do not print environment files, tokens, or private keys while inspecting the runner. ## Mac SSH access The Mac private key stays at `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`. messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D boxing game in the empty PlayGround repo: **TG BOXING – THE GLORY OF CHAMPIONS**, with career mode, character customization, belts/rankings, NPC AI, dynamic news, TG COIN economy, and real multiplayer by invite link.

## Requirements
- Fully functional (no decorative buttons); every menu working, career persistence, fights with start/development/result, AI, rankings updates, news from real game data, conquerable belts.
- Real multiplayer between two devices using backend/WebSocket or equivalent; create room, share link, private/public rooms, room code, reconnection, input/score sync. Explicitly not local two-character simulation.
- 3D: detailed customizable characters, fluid animations, expressions, sweat/impact effects, dynamic arena lighting, animated crowd, referee/coaches, cinematic cameras, KO camera, replays, entrances, victory/defeat animations.
- 100+ customization options per applicable category: hair, shorts, tops, shoes, robes, gloves, colorways; 100+ NPCs; 11 weight classes; rankings TOP 100; multiple fictional organizations and belt tiers.
- Career: create fighter, nationality, contracts/offers, purses, training, gym, reputation, calendar, title defenses, rivalries, interviews, awards, trophies, news, stats.
- TG COIN earned/spent, optional wagers with basic fraud protection, virtual only; fictional training boosters (not real substances).
- 15 arenas; mobile-friendly 60 FPS target, touch controls with customizable size/position; keyboard/mouse support.
- Portuguese UI, original identity inspired by anime boxing energy but with original characters/visuals.
- Build request instruction: do not ask clarifying questions; make assumptions and note them at finish. Save small JPEG screenshots for checks, viewport ≤1280px.

## Decisions
- Vanilla JS + Vite + Three.js + PeerJS; procedural 3D models/textures/audio (no external art assets) to keep everything self-contained.
- Static deployment: PeerJS cloud (`0.peerjs.com`, verified reachable) for real WebRTC multiplayer signaling, since the runtime only serves static `dist`; invite URL format `?room=CODE`.
- Host-authoritative multiplayer design; guest sends inputs, host sends snapshots at ~20 Hz; public quick-match via deterministic PeerJS room slots planned.
- Universe of 1,100 NPCs (100 × 11 divisions), deterministically generated; universe persisted separately from career save.
- Combat: stamina/guard/counters/dodge windows, 4 punches + body, knockdown/recovery taps, judges’ decision, KO/TKO/DRAW/QUIT.
- All visuals generated in-browser (CanvasTexture patterns, procedural boxers, crowd InstancedMesh, synth WebAudio).

## Work State
### Completed
- Project scaffold: `package.json`, dependencies installed (`three`, `peerjs`, `vite`); self-hosted Bebas Neue/Barlow fonts in `public/fonts`.
- `src/core/rng.js`, `src/core/data.js` (catalogs incl. 100 hair/shorts/tops/shoes/robes/gloves/colorways, 11 divisions, 3 orgs, 7 belt tiers, 15 arenas, shop items, awards, achievements, quotes).
- `src/core/store.js` (save schema, persistence, economy, settings, achievements, player fighter adapter).
- `src/core/universe.js` (NPC generation, rankings, offers/negotiation, background simulation, news generation, record books/awards).
- `src/core/appearance.js` (deterministic NPC appearance).
- `src/three/textures.js` (procedural ring/apron/banner/pattern/spark/belt textures).
- `src/three/boxer.js` (procedural rigged boxer, 20 hair shapes, beards, faces, shorts/gloves/shoes/robes, expressions, pose/animation, KO fall, victory, render-state capture, staff and 3D belt factory).
- `src/three/environment.js` (championship ring, crowd instancing, 15 arena dressing variants, gym, showcase menu scene, editor studio).
- `src/game/fight.js` (combat engine, AI, judges, knockdowns, snapshots/remote input, quick simulation).
- `src/game/fightview.js` (cinematic cameras, entrance, referee/staff, hit sparks, sweat, KO camera, replay recording/playback, confetti, 3D belt victory).
- `src/game/audio.js` (procedural punches, bell, crowd, music, UI sounds).
- `src/ui/icons.js`, `src/ui/styles.css` (full dark/crimson/gold visual system, responsive layouts, fight HUD, editor, lobby, results).
- `src/app.js` (renderer, scene backgrounds menu/editor/gym/fight, navigation and animation loop).

### Active
- UI screen implementations and wiring: `main.js`, menu, career dashboard, editor, rankings, news, shop, gym, stats/awards, settings, fight UI/HUD, multiplayer UI, modals/toasts.
- `index.html` and Vite entry not yet written.
- Multiplayer networking module not yet written.
- No build/test/screenshots run yet.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Create `index.html` (canvas `#game-canvas`, `#ui-root`, boot markup) and `src/main.js` boot flow/loading overlay.
2. Implement screens in `src/ui/` (menu first, then career, editor, rankings/news/shop/gym/stats/settings), wired to `App.navigate`.
3. Implement `src/ui/fight-ui.js` (pre-fight VS card, entrance button, HUD, keyboard/touch controls with queued punch inputs, round/knockdown overlays, pause, replay, result and career consequences).
4. Implement multiplayer (`peerjs`) + lobby UI and test two tabs/room invite.
5. Fix known issues: `computeAwards` in `universe.js` references `AWARD_TYPES` without import; verify boxer arm/guard poses and KO body offset via screenshots; engine `endFight` ordering during knockdown (`updateKnockdown` sets phase `ko` after `endFight`).
6. Run `npm run build`, Playwright screenshots (menu/editor/fight/rankings/multiplayer), fix runtime errors, save small JPEGs ≤1280px.
7. Add unit/smoke tests (`tests/*.test.mjs`), README with backend/multiplayer setup notes and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/core/data.js`: all catalogs/constants (divisions, orgs, belts, arenas, items).
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/core/store.js`: save schema/persistence API; essential for UI writes.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/core/universe.js`: rankings/offers/news functions; note missing `AWARD_TYPES` import.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game/fight.js`: combat engine API (`FightEngine`, `BoxingAI`, `PUNCHES`).
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game/fightview.js`: render/replay/belt API used by fight UI.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/app.js`: `App` singleton, background scene switching, navigate/frame hooks.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/ui/styles.css`: existing class names to reuse for all screens/HUD.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/ui/icons.js`: `icon(name,size)` helper.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/three/boxer.js`: boxer construction/animation; needs visual tuning.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/three/environment.js`: arena/gym/studio builders.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game/audio.js`: `SoundEngine` API and event handler.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/core/appearance.js`: `appearanceForFighter`, `appearanceForPlayer`, `randomAppearance`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/package.json`: scripts `dev` (port 3002), `build`, `test`.

## Important Context
- Repo was empty except process/runtime scripts; all game code is new and **uncommitted**.
- Current date/environment: Nov 11 2026; use `npm run dev` on port 3002 for checks and `playwright-cli` with headed Chromium/SwiftShader per project docs.
- `default-start.mjs` only serves static Vite output; no custom backend will be deployed, so PeerJS cloud is the practical real-multiplayer transport. Test connectivity to `https://0.peerjs.com/peerjs/id` (confirmed working) and `unpkg` (200).
- `start.sh`/`capture.sh` currently use runtime default scripts; Vite detection will run `npm ci/install`, `vite build --base ./`, serve `dist`.
- Visual reference screenshots (Undisputed-style UI/gameplay) were fetched to `/tmp/opencode/*.png`; not part of the project.
- `src/game/fightview.js` uses `VISUAL_SCALE = 0.68` to map engine positions to world and relies on `view.update()` + engine updates driven externally; replay frames are recorded internally.
- Fight engine starts in `intro` phase; call `engine.start()` after entrance. `FightScreen` must consume `engine.drainEvents()` each frame and pass to `view.handleEvent()` and `audio.handleEvents()`.
- `App` exposes `navigator`, `setFrame`, `showMenu`, `showEditor`, `showGym`, `showFight`, `saveNow`, `quality`, `audio`, `save`, `universe`.
- Need to support invite deep link `?room=CODE` at boot and copy-link UX (`location.origin + location.pathname + '?room=' + code`).
- Multiplayer wagers: plan idempotent result application via match ID; host validates declared balances; virtual-only disclaimer.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D boxing game in the empty PlayGround repo: **TG BOXING – THE GLORY OF CHAMPIONS**, with career mode, character customization, belts/rankings, NPC AI, dynamic news, TG COIN economy, and real multiplayer by invite link.

## Requirements
- Fully functional (no decorative buttons); every menu working, career persistence, fights with start/development/result, AI, rankings updates, news from real game data, conquerable belts.
- Real multiplayer between two devices using backend/WebSocket or equivalent; create room, share link, private/public rooms, room code, reconnection, input/score sync. Explicitly not local two-character simulation.
- 3D: detailed customizable characters, fluid animations, expressions, sweat/impact effects, dynamic arena lighting, animated crowd, referee/coaches, cinematic cameras, KO camera, replays, entrances, victory/defeat animations.
- 100+ customization options per applicable category: hair, shorts, tops, shoes, robes, gloves, colorways; 100+ NPCs; 11 weight classes; rankings TOP 100; multiple fictional organizations and belt tiers.
- Career: create fighter, nationality, contracts/offers, purses, training, gym, reputation, calendar, title defenses, rivalries, interviews, awards, trophies, news, stats.
- TG COIN earned/spent, optional wagers with basic fraud protection, virtual only; fictional training boosters (not real substances).
- 15 arenas; mobile-friendly 60 FPS target, touch controls with customizable size/position; keyboard/mouse support.
- Portuguese UI, original identity inspired by anime boxing energy but with original characters/visuals.
- Build request instruction: do not ask clarifying questions; make assumptions and note them at finish. Save small JPEG screenshots for checks, viewport ≤1280px.

## Decisions
- Vanilla JS + Vite + Three.js + PeerJS; procedural 3D models/textures/audio (no external art assets) to keep everything self-contained.
- Static deployment: PeerJS cloud (`0.peerjs.com`, verified reachable) for real WebRTC multiplayer signaling, since the runtime only serves static `dist`; invite URL format `?room=CODE`.
- Host-authoritative multiplayer: host is p1 and simulates, guest is p2 and sends inputs; host broadcasts snapshots (~15 Hz) and events. Public quick-match via deterministic PeerJS room slots `tgboxing-v1-open-0..7`; private rooms via `tgboxing-v1-p-<CODE>`.
- Universe of 1,100 NPCs (100 × 11 divisions), deterministically generated; universe persisted separately from career save.
- Combat: stamina/guard/counters/dodge windows, 4 punches + body, knockdown/recovery taps, judges’ decision, KO/TKO/DRAW/QUIT.
- All visuals generated in-browser (CanvasTexture patterns, procedural boxers, crowd InstancedMesh, synth WebAudio).
- Career results are idempotent via `result.matchId` stored in `career.appliedMatches`; title changes, news, purses, achievements applied once.
- Wagers planned as virtual-only, balance-checked, capped, with match receipt hash and per-match idempotency.

## Work State
### Completed
- Project scaffold: `package.json`, dependencies installed (`three`, `peerjs`, `vite`); self-hosted fonts in `public/fonts`.
- Core engine: `rng.js`, `data.js` (100 hair/shorts/tops/shoes/robes/gloves/colorways, 11 divisions, 3 orgs, 7 belt tiers, 15 arenas, shop, awards, achievements, quotes), `store.js`, `universe.js`, `appearance.js`.
- 3D layer: `textures.js`, `boxer.js`, `environment.js`, `fightview.js`.
- Game layer: `fight.js` (engine/AI/judges/knockdowns/snapshots), `audio.js`.
- UI foundation: `icons.js`, `styles.css` (full visual system), `app.js`.
- Added `index.html`, `src/main.js` not yet written; wait—`index.html`/`main.js` still pending (see Active).
- New core career operations: `src/core/career.js` with offers, negotiation accept/decline/cancel, drills, rest, fight result application, titles, news, achievements, awards.
- Fixed `AWARD_TYPES` missing import in `universe.js`.
- Added save fields `activeOffer`, `appliedMatches`, `boosters` and settings defaults (`muted`, `showHints`, `highContrast`).
- UI shell: `src/ui/shell.js` (routing, topbar, wallet, toasts, modals, confirm, cleanup hooks, backgrounds).
- Helpers: `src/ui/helpers.js`.
- Screens implemented: `menu.js`, `create.js`, `editor.js`, `career.js`, `rankings.js`, `news.js`, `shop.js`, `gym.js`, `stats.js`, `settings.js`.
- Networking module: `src/net/net.js` (PeerJS host/guest, private/public rooms, hello/welcome, reconnect, heartbeat, invite URL, receipt hash).

### Active
- Multiplayer lobby/UI (`src/ui/screens/multiplayer.js`) and fight screen (`src/ui/screens/fight.js`) still to implement.
- `index.html` and `src/main.js` boot flow still to implement.
- Wire screens into shell/main and test build.
- Additional CSS for new classes (create screen, alloc grid, offer actions, gym/drill/timing, dossier/history/achievement cards, champ rows, etc.).
- Visual tuning of boxer poses, arm/guard, KO body offset; fix `endFight`/`updateKnockdown` phase ordering if needed.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Create `index.html` (canvas `#game-canvas`, `#ui-root`, boot screen, toast stack) and `src/main.js` (import styles, App boot, load save/universe, seed news, register screens, deep-link `?room=CODE`, boot progress, beforeunload save).
2. Implement `src/ui/screens/multiplayer.js`: create/join private, public quick match, share/copy invite link, room code, ready states, wager selector with validation, chat/status, reconnect UI, start host/guest fight.
3. Implement `src/ui/screens/fight.js`: pre-fight VS/entrance, HUD, keyboard + touch controls, knockdown get-up, pause/replay, result overlay, career consequences, title belt, multiplayer snapshot/input sync.
4. Add missing CSS and verify responsiveness at ≤1280px.
5. Run `npm run build`, Playwright screenshots (menu/editor/fight/rankings/multiplayer), fix runtime errors, save small JPEGs.
6. Add tests (`tests/*.test.mjs`), README with multiplayer/backend assumptions, note assumptions at finish.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/ui/shell.js`: routing, topbar, toast/modal API used by all screens.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/ui/screens/career.js`: dashboard and offer/fight wiring.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/core/career.js`: career operations and result application.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/net/net.js`: real PeerJS networking protocol.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game/fight.js`: combat engine API/snapshots.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game/fightview.js`: cinematic view, entrance/replay/belt.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/core/store.js`: save schema/persistence.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/core/universe.js`: rankings/offers/news/awards.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/ui/styles.css`: visual system, needs appended classes.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/app.js`: renderer, scene backgrounds, frame hooks.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/ui/screens/editor.js`: 100+ customization categories.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/ui/screens/create.js`: career creation flow.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/core/data.js`: all catalogs/constants.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game/audio.js`: SoundEngine API/events.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/package.json`: scripts `dev` (3002), `build`, `test`.

## Important Context
- Repo was empty except process/runtime scripts; all game code is new and **uncommitted**.
- No `src/main.js` / `index.html` yet, so app currently cannot run or build meaningfully.
- `FightEngine` starts in `intro`; call `engine.start()` after entrance. Consume `engine.drainEvents()` each frame and pass to `view.handleEvent()` + `audio.handleEvents()`.
- App exposes `navigator`, `setFrame`, `showMenu`, `showEditor`, `showGym`, `showFight`, `saveNow`, `quality`, `audio`, `save`, `universe`.
- `FightView` uses `VISUAL_SCALE = 0.68`; host must drive `engine.update(dt, {p1,p2})`; guest applies `applySnapshot` and does not simulate.
- Existing `styles.css` class names should be reused; many new screen-specific classes still need CSS.
- UI must remain Portuguese; TG COIN virtual-only disclaimer required in shop/settings/multiplayer wagers.
- Use `npm run dev` on port 3002 and Playwright with headed Chromium/SwiftShader per project docs; capture JPEG screenshots ≤1280px.
- PeerJS cloud connectivity to `https://0.peerjs.com/peerjs/id` previously confirmed working; no TURN server, so some strict NATs may fail.

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D boxing game in the empty PlayGround repo: **TG BOXING – THE GLORY OF CHAMPIONS**, with career mode, character customization, belts/rankings, NPC AI, dynamic news, TG COIN economy, and real multiplayer by invite link.

## Requirements
- Fully functional (no decorative buttons); every menu working, career persistence, fights with start/development/result, AI, rankings updates, news from real game data, conquerable belts.
- Real multiplayer between two devices using backend/WebSocket or equivalent; create room, share link, private/public rooms, room code, reconnection, input/score sync. Explicitly not local two-character simulation.
- 3D: detailed customizable characters, fluid animations, expressions, sweat/impact effects, dynamic arena lighting, animated crowd, referee/coaches, cinematic cameras, KO camera, replays, entrances, victory/defeat animations.
- 100+ customization options per applicable category: hair, shorts, tops, shoes, robes, gloves, colorways; 100+ NPCs; 11 weight classes; rankings TOP 100; multiple fictional organizations and belt tiers.
- Career: create fighter, nationality, contracts/offers, purses, training, gym, reputation, calendar, title defenses, rivalries, interviews, awards, trophies, news, stats.
- TG COIN earned/spent, optional wagers with basic fraud protection, virtual only; fictional training boosters (not real substances).
- 15 arenas; mobile-friendly 60 FPS target, touch controls with customizable size/position; keyboard/mouse support.
- Portuguese UI, original identity inspired by anime boxing energy but with original characters/visuals.
- Build request instruction: do not ask clarifying questions; make assumptions and note them at finish. Save small JPEG screenshots for checks, viewport ≤1280px.

## Decisions
- Vanilla JS + Vite + Three.js + PeerJS; procedural 3D models/textures/audio (no external art assets) to keep everything self-contained.
- Static deployment: PeerJS cloud (`0.peerjs.com`, verified reachable) for real WebRTC multiplayer signaling, since runtime only serves static `dist`; invite URL format `?room=CODE`.
- Host-authoritative multiplayer: host is p1 and simulates; guest is p2 and sends inputs; host broadcasts snapshots (~15 Hz) and events. Public quick-match via deterministic PeerJS room slots `tgboxing-v1-open-0..7`; private rooms via `tgboxing-v1-p-<CODE>`.
- Universe of 1,100 NPCs (100 × 11 divisions), deterministically generated; universe persisted separately from career save.
- Combat: stamina/guard/counters/dodge windows, 4 punches + body, knockdown/recovery taps, judges’ decision, KO/TKO/DRAW/QUIT.
- All visuals generated in-browser (CanvasTexture patterns, procedural boxers, crowd InstancedMesh, synth WebAudio).
- Career results are idempotent via `result.matchId` stored in `career.appliedMatches`; title changes, news, purses, achievements applied once.
- Wagers planned as virtual-only, balance-checked, capped, with match receipt hash and per-match idempotency.
- Multiplayer match config will be built by host after both ready: shared `matchId`, arena, rounds, wager = min(both players’ chosen wagers), host/guest fighter profiles.
- Multiplayer fight flow: host drives combat and broadcasts snapshots/events; guest applies snapshots and sends inputs; reconnect pauses both briefly and host resends snapshot on rejoin.
- Fight screen will show host/p1 on left and guest/p2 on right regardless of local perspective; each player controls their assigned slot.

## Work State
### Completed
- Project scaffold: `package.json`, dependencies installed (`three`, `peerjs`, `vite`); self-hosted fonts in `public/fonts`.
- Core engine: `rng.js`, `data.js` (100 hair/shorts/tops/shoes/robes/gloves/colorways, 11 divisions, 3 orgs, 7 belt tiers, 15 arenas, shop, awards, achievements, quotes), `store.js`, `universe.js`, `appearance.js`.
- 3D layer: `textures.js`, `boxer.js`, `environment.js`, `fightview.js`.
- Game layer: `fight.js` (engine/AI/judges/knockdowns/snapshots), `audio.js`.
- UI foundation: `icons.js`, `styles.css` (substantial visual system), `app.js`.
- Core career operations: `src/core/career.js` with offers, negotiation accept/decline/cancel, drills, rest, fight result application, titles, news, achievements, awards.
- Fixed `AWARD_TYPES` missing import in `universe.js`.
- Added save fields `activeOffer`, `appliedMatches`, `boosters` and settings defaults (`muted`, `showHints`, `highContrast`).
- UI shell: `src/ui/shell.js` (routing, topbar, wallet, toasts, modals, confirm, cleanup hooks, backgrounds).
- Helpers: `src/ui/helpers.js`.
- Screens implemented: `menu.js`, `create.js`, `editor.js`, `career.js`, `rankings.js`, `news.js`, `shop.js`, `gym.js`, `stats.js`, `settings.js`.
- Networking module: `src/net/net.js` (PeerJS host/guest, private/public rooms, hello/welcome, reconnect, heartbeat, invite URL, receipt hash).
- Created `index.html` with `#game-canvas`, `#ui-root`, boot screen, toast stack, favicon, no-script fallback, module entry `/src/main.js`.

### Active
- `src/main.js` boot flow still to implement.
- Multiplayer lobby/UI (`src/ui/screens/multiplayer.js`) and fight screen (`src/ui/screens/fight.js`) still to implement.
- Wire screens into shell/main and test build.
- Additional CSS for new classes (create screen, alloc grid, offer actions, gym/drill/timing, dossier/history/achievement cards, champ rows, news article, lobby chat/rules, etc.).
- Patch `src/net/net.js` host reconnect logic: currently `_bindConnection` rejects replacement host connections when stale `this.conn` exists; should accept if `!this.connected`.
- Visual tuning of boxer poses, arm/guard, KO body offset; fix `endFight`/`updateKnockdown` phase ordering if needed.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Create `src/main.js`: import styles, instantiate `App`/`UI`, load save/universe, seed news, register all screens, handle deep-link `?room=CODE`, boot progress, audio unlock, beforeunload save, and expose debug handle if useful.
2. Implement `src/ui/screens/multiplayer.js`: create/join private, public quick match, share/copy invite link, room code, ready states, wager selector with validation, chat/status, reconnect UI, host builds match config then both navigate to fight.
3. Implement `src/ui/screens/fight.js`: pre-fight VS/entrance, HUD, keyboard + touch + mouse controls, knockdown get-up, pause/replay, result overlay, career consequences, title belt, multiplayer snapshot/input sync and reconnect handling.

- Game code is new and **uncommitted**; repo originally only had process/runtime scripts and docs.

- `FightEngine` starts in `intro`; call `engine.start()` after entrance. Consume `engine.drainEvents()` each frame and pass to `view.handleEvent()` + `audio.handleEvents()`.

- `applyFightResult` is idempotent by `result.matchId`; career `p1` is player and `winnerId==='p1'` means win.
- UI must remain Portuguese; TG COIN virtual-only disclaimer required in shop/settings/multiplayer wagers.
- PeerJS cloud works for signaling but there is no TURN server, so some strict NATs may fail; public rooms limited to `OPEN-0..7`.

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.

- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D boxing game in the empty PlayGround repo: **TG BOXING – THE GLORY OF CHAMPIONS**, with career mode, character customization, belts/rankings, NPC AI, dynamic news, TG COIN economy, and real multiplayer by invite link.

## Requirements
- Fully functional (no decorative buttons); every menu working, career persistence, fights with start/development/result, AI, rankings updates, news from real game data, conquerable belts.
- Real multiplayer between two devices using backend/WebSocket or equivalent; create room, share link, private/public rooms, room code, reconnection, input/score sync. Explicitly not local two-character simulation.
- 3D: detailed customizable characters, fluid animations, expressions, sweat/impact effects, dynamic arena lighting, animated crowd, referee/coaches, cinematic cameras, KO camera, replays, entrances, victory/defeat animations.
- 100+ customization options per applicable category: hair, shorts, tops, shoes, robes, gloves, colorways; 100+ NPCs; 11 weight classes; rankings TOP 100; multiple fictional organizations and belt tiers.
- Career: create fighter, nationality, contracts/offers, purses, training, gym, reputation, calendar, title defenses, rivalries, interviews, awards, trophies, news, stats.
- TG COIN earned/spent, optional wagers with basic fraud protection, virtual only; fictional training boosters (not real substances).
- 15 arenas; mobile-friendly 60 FPS target, touch controls with customizable size/position; keyboard/mouse support.
- Portuguese UI, original identity inspired by anime boxing energy but with original characters/visuals.
- Build request instruction: do not ask clarifying questions; make assumptions and note them at finish. Save small JPEG screenshots for checks, viewport ≤1280px.

## Decisions
- Vanilla JS + Vite + Three.js + PeerJS; procedural 3D models/textures/audio (no external art assets) to keep everything self-contained.
- Static deployment: PeerJS cloud (`0.peerjs.com`) for real WebRTC multiplayer signaling, since runtime only serves static `dist`; invite URL format `?room=CODE`.
- Host-authoritative multiplayer: host is p1 and simulates; guest is p2 and sends inputs; host broadcasts snapshots (~15 Hz) and events. Public quick-match via deterministic PeerJS room slots `tgboxing-v1-open-0..7`; private rooms via `tgboxing-v1-p-<CODE>`.
- Universe of 1,100 NPCs (100 × 11 divisions), deterministically generated; universe persisted separately from career save.
- Combat: stamina/guard/counters/dodge windows, 4 punches + body, knockdown/recovery taps, judges’ decision, KO/TKO/DRAW/QUIT.
- All visuals generated in-browser (CanvasTexture patterns, procedural boxers, crowd InstancedMesh, synth WebAudio).
- Career results are idempotent via `result.matchId` stored in `career.appliedMatches`; title changes, news, purses, achievements applied once.
- Wagers planned as virtual-only, capped (500 TG), effective wager = min(both players’ choices), balance-checked, with match receipt hash and per-match idempotency.
- Multiplayer match config built by host after both ready: shared `matchId`, arena, rounds, wager, host/guest fighter profiles; guest receives `match` message and launches fight.
- Multiplayer fight flow: host drives combat and broadcasts snapshots/events; guest applies snapshots and sends inputs; reconnect pauses both briefly and host resends snapshot on rejoin.
- Fight screen shows host/p1 on left and guest/p2 on right regardless of local perspective; each player controls their assigned slot.
- Anonymous online players get a balanced generated fighter; signed-in career players use profile attributes/appearance/record.

## Work State
### Completed
- Project scaffold: `package.json`, dependencies installed (`three`, `peerjs`, `vite`); self-hosted fonts in `public/fonts`.
- Core engine: `rng.js`, `data.js` (100 hair/shorts/tops/shoes/robes/gloves/colorways, 11 divisions, 3 orgs, 7 belt tiers, 15 arenas, shop, awards, achievements, quotes), `store.js`, `universe.js`, `appearance.js`.
- 3D layer: `textures.js`, `boxer.js`, `environment.js`, `fightview.js`.
- Game layer: `fight.js` (engine/AI/judges/knockdowns/snapshots), `audio.js`.
- UI foundation: `icons.js`, `styles.css` (substantial visual system), `app.js`.
- Core career operations: `src/core/career.js` with offers, negotiation accept/decline/cancel, drills, rest, fight result application, titles, news, achievements, awards.
- Fixed `AWARD_TYPES` missing import in `universe.js`.
- Save fields `activeOffer`, `appliedMatches`, `boosters`; settings defaults (`muted`, `showHints`, `highContrast`).
- UI shell: `src/ui/shell.js` (routing, topbar, wallet, toasts, modals, confirm, cleanup hooks, backgrounds).
- Helpers: `src/ui/helpers.js`.
- Screens implemented: `menu.js`, `create.js`, `editor.js`, `career.js`, `rankings.js`, `news.js`, `shop.js`, `gym.js`, `stats.js`, `settings.js`.
- Networking module: `src/net/net.js` (PeerJS host/guest, private/public rooms, hello/welcome, reconnect, heartbeat, invite URL, receipt hash).
- Created `index.html` with `#game-canvas`, `#ui-root`, boot screen, toast stack, favicon, no-script fallback, module entry `/src/main.js`.
- Fixed wrong relative imports in all `src/ui/screens/*.js` from `./icons.js`/`./helpers.js` to `../icons.js`/`../helpers.js`.
- Patched `src/net/net.js`: accept replacement host connection when `!this.connected`; call open handler immediately if `conn.open` (fixes guest hello never being sent); added `joinPublicSlot`, `joinByCode`; reconnect timer guard; `everConnected`/resume tracking.
- Implemented `src/main.js`: loads save/universe, generates universe if missing, seeds news/offers, registers all screens, deep-link `?room=CODE`, boot progress hide, audio unlock, autosave/visibility/beforeunload, global errors, debug `window.TG_BOXING`.
- Implemented `src/ui/screens/multiplayer.js`: private/public rooms, create/quick/join, invite copy, room code, ready/wager/settings handshake, chat, reconnect/error UI, host builds match and navigates fight, session persistence across lobby↔fight, fighter info sanitization and helpers (`getMp`, `sendMp`, `attachMp`, `closeMp`, `mpFighterDef`, `localFighterInfo`, `sanitizeFighterInfo`).

### Active
- `src/ui/screens/fight.js` still missing (not yet created); app cannot yet import/run.
- CSS additions still needed for new classes (`create-*`, `alloc-*`, `offer-actions`, `active-contract`, `belts-strip`, `champ-row`, `dossier`, `article-meta/hero`, `news-cat-row`, `drill-grid`, `timing-*`, `training-gain`, `history-row`, `result-badge`, `timeline`, `mp-identity`, `join-row`, `wager-box`, `chat-panel`, `mp-disclaimer`, `fight` adjustments, responsive).
- Visual tuning of boxer poses, arm/guard, KO body offset; fix `endFight`/`updateKnockdown` phase ordering if needed.
- Verify build and runtime; no tests or README yet.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement `src/ui/screens/fight.js`: intro/VS entrance, HUD, keyboard/mouse + touch controls (joystick + punch/block/dodge/get-up, customizable size/side/opacity), pause/replay, result overlay, career consequences/title belt/news, multiplayer snapshot/input sync, reconnect pause/resync, wager settlement/receipt.
2. Wire fight result buttons/rematch and `ui.mpKeep` cleanup behavior; ensure active career offer result applied exactly once.
3. Add missing CSS (create/editor/shop/multiplayer/fight/utility classes) and responsive rules at ≤1280px.
4. Run `npm run build`, fix import/runtime errors, then Playwright screenshots (menu/editor/fight/rankings/multiplayer/result), save small JPEGs.
5. Add tests (`tests/*.test.mjs`) and README documenting multiplayer/backend assumptions, PeerJS cloud/no TURN limitation, virtual TG COIN, and note assumptions at finish.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/ui/screens/fight.js`: missing; next core deliverable.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/ui/screens/multiplayer.js`: lobby, handshake, helpers used by fight screen.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/net/net.js`: PeerJS API/events, joinByCode, reconnection behavior.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game/fight.js`: `FightEngine`, snapshots/inputs/events, AI, result.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game/fightview.js`: cinematic view, entrance/replay/belt; `VISUAL_SCALE = 0.68`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/ui/screens/career.js`: navigates `fight` with `{mode:'career', offer, arenaId, rounds, division}`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/core/career.js`: `applyFightResult` consequences/idempotency.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/core/store.js`: save schema, `persist`, `createPlayerFighter`, settings.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/ui/styles.css`: visual system; needs appended missing classes.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/ui/shell.js`: routing, cleanup, topbar, toast/modal API.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js`: boot and screen registration.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/core/data.js`: catalogs, `ARENA_BY_ID`, `DIVISION_BY_ID`, defaults.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/ui/helpers.js`: `esc`, `h`, formatting, `screenHead`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game/audio.js`: `SoundEngine` event handling.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/app.js`: renderer/background loop, `showFight`, quality.

## Important Context
- Game code is new and **uncommitted**; repo originally only had process/runtime scripts and docs.
- `src/main.js` currently imports `src/ui/screens/multiplayer.js` and `src/ui/screens/fight.js`; build fails until `fight.js` exists.
- `FightEngine` starts in `intro`; call `engine.start()` after entrance. Drain `engine.drainEvents()` each frame and pass to `view.handleEvent()` + `audio.handleEvents()`.
- `FightView` constructor: `new FightView({ renderer, engine, arenaConfig, quality, appearances:{p1,p2}, mobile })`; then `ui.app.showFight(view)`.
- To simulate before rendering, wrap `view.update` before `app.showFight(view)`; `App.loop` calls background update then frame hook.
- Host must drive `engine.update(dt, {p1,p2})`; guest must only apply snapshots, send inputs, and not simulate.
- `applyFightResult({ save, universe, result, offer, division, arenaId })`; career p1 is player, `winnerId==='p1'` means win; idempotent via `result.matchId`.
- `FightView.syncFighters` uses `engine.phase`, `engine.result`, `engine.down`; `showBelt(belt)` defers until `phase==='end'`; replay frames only recorded after intro.
- Multiplayer session in `ui.mp` (`session`, `role`, `match`, `listeners`, `localInfo`, ready/wager state); `ui.mpKeep = true` prevents lobby cleanup from destroying session when navigating to fight.
- PeerJS cloud works for signaling but no TURN server; strict NATs may fail; public rooms limited to `OPEN-0..7`.
- Use `npm run dev` on port 3002 and Playwright headed Chromium/SwiftShader per project docs; capture JPEG screenshots ≤1280px.
- `capture.sh` uses runtime default capture; `start.sh` uses runtime default start.
- Settings screen uses `data-nav` for local section buttons, which may trigger harmless unknown-screen warnings; consider renaming to `data-section` while adding CSS.
- Anonymous online fighter uses 58 in each attribute and `randomAppearance('tg-online-challenger')`; local career fighter uses profile data.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D boxing game in the empty PlayGround repo: **TG BOXING – THE GLORY OF CHAMPIONS**, with career mode, character customization, belts/rankings, NPC AI, dynamic news, TG COIN economy, and real multiplayer by invite link.

## Requirements
- Fully functional (no decorative buttons); every menu working, career persistence, fights with start/development/result, AI, rankings updates, news from real game data, conquerable belts.
- Real multiplayer between two devices using backend/WebSocket or equivalent; create room, share link, private/public rooms, room code, reconnection, input/score sync. Explicitly not local two-character simulation.
- 3D: detailed customizable characters, fluid animations, expressions, sweat/impact effects, dynamic arena lighting, animated crowd, referee/coaches, cinematic cameras, KO camera, replays, entrances, victory/defeat animations.
- 100+ customization options per applicable category: hair, shorts, tops, shoes, robes, gloves, colorways; 100+ NPCs; 11 weight classes; rankings TOP 100; multiple fictional organizations and belt tiers.
- Career: create fighter, nationality, contracts/offers, purses, training, gym, reputation, calendar, title defenses, rivalries, interviews, awards, trophies, news, stats.
- TG COIN earned/spent, optional wagers with basic fraud protection, virtual only; fictional training boosters (not real substances).
- 15 arenas; mobile-friendly 60 FPS target, touch controls with customizable size/position; keyboard/mouse support.
- Portuguese UI, original identity inspired by anime boxing energy but with original characters/visuals.
- Build request instruction: do not ask clarifying questions; make assumptions and note them at finish. Save small JPEG screenshots for checks, viewport ≤1280px.

## Decisions
- Vanilla JS + Vite + Three.js + PeerJS; procedural 3D models/textures/audio (no external art assets) to keep everything self-contained.
- Static deployment: PeerJS cloud (`0.peerjs.com`) for real WebRTC multiplayer signaling, since runtime only serves static `dist`; invite URL format `?room=CODE`.
- Host-authoritative multiplayer: host is p1 and simulates; guest is p2 and sends inputs; host broadcasts snapshots (~15 Hz) and events. Public quick-match via deterministic PeerJS room slots `tgboxing-v1-open-0..7`; private rooms via `tgboxing-v1-p-<CODE>`.
- Universe of 1,100 NPCs (100 × 11 divisions), deterministically generated; universe persisted separately from career save.
- Combat: stamina/guard/counters/dodge windows, 4 punches + body, knockdown/recovery taps, judges’ decision, KO/TKO/DRAW/QUIT.
- All visuals generated in-browser (CanvasTexture patterns, procedural boxers, crowd InstancedMesh, synth WebAudio).
- Career results are idempotent via `result.matchId` stored in `career.appliedMatches`; title changes, news, purses, achievements applied once.
- Wagers virtual-only, capped (500 TG), effective wager = min(both players’ choices), balance-checked, with match receipt hash and per-match idempotency.
- Multiplayer match config built by host after both ready: shared `matchId`, arena, rounds, wager, host/guest fighter profiles; guest receives `match` message and launches fight.
- Multiplayer fight flow: host drives combat and broadcasts snapshots/events; guest applies snapshots and sends inputs; reconnect pauses both briefly and host resends snapshot on rejoin.
- Fight screen shows host/p1 on left and guest/p2 on right regardless of local perspective; each player controls their assigned slot.
- Anonymous online players get a balanced generated fighter; signed-in career players use profile attributes/appearance/record.
- Multiplayer session events renamed from `'ready'` to `'room'` to avoid collision with peer `{t:'ready'}` handshake messages.

## Work State
### Completed
- Project scaffold: `package.json`, dependencies installed (`three`, `peerjs`, `vite`); self-hosted fonts in `public/fonts`.
- Core engine: `rng.js`, `data.js` (100 hair/shorts/tops/shoes/robes/gloves/colorways, 11 divisions, 3 orgs, 7 belt tiers, 15 arenas, shop, awards, achievements, quotes), `store.js`, `universe.js`, `appearance.js`.
- 3D layer: `textures.js`, `boxer.js`, `environment.js`, `fightview.js`.
- Game layer: `fight.js` (engine/AI/judges/knockdowns/snapshots), `audio.js`.
- UI foundation: `icons.js`, `styles.css` (substantial visual system), `app.js`.
- Core career operations: `src/core/career.js` with offers, negotiation accept/decline/cancel, drills, rest, fight result application, titles, news, achievements, awards.
- UI shell: `src/ui/shell.js` (routing, topbar, wallet, toasts, modals, confirm, cleanup hooks, backgrounds).
- Helpers: `src/ui/helpers.js`.
- Screens implemented: `menu.js`, `create.js`, `editor.js`, `career.js`, `rankings.js`, `news.js`, `shop.js`, `gym.js`, `stats.js`, `settings.js`, `multiplayer.js`.
- Networking module: `src/net/net.js` (PeerJS host/guest, private/public rooms, hello/welcome, reconnect, heartbeat, invite URL, receipt hash).
- `src/main.js` boot, screen registration, deep-link `?room=CODE`, save/universe persistence, debug `window.TG_BOXING`.
- Multiplayer lobby with private/public rooms, invite copy, code join, ready/wager/settings handshake, chat, reconnect/error UI.
- **Created `src/ui/screens/fight.js`** with cinematic VS intro/entrance, HUD, keyboard + mouse + touch controls, pause/replay, result overlay, career consequences, title belt display, multiplayer snapshot/input sync, reconnect handling, wager settlement/receipt, and get-up taps.
- Added `pause` icon to `src/ui/icons.js`.
- Fixed duplicate `case 'ready'` bug by renaming NetSession room-ready events to `'room'` in `src/net/net.js` and `src/ui/screens/multiplayer.js`.
- Class lists in fight screen reference existing CSS plus a new set still needing CSS: `fight-screen`, `fight-intro-wrap`, `intro-kicker`, `vs-tags`, `intro-quote`, `intro-hint`, `network-chip`, `getup-btn`, `result-tags`, `result-fighters`, `result-rewards`, `reward`, `mono`, `reconnect-banner`, `urgent`, `hidden`, `act-btn.body`.

### Active
- CSS additions still needed for new fight classes (`fight-screen`, `hidden`, `fight-ui` pointer-events overrides, touch side/opacity/scale, `act-btn.body`, `getup-btn`, `network-chip`, intro extras, reconnect banner, result rewards/tags/fighters, replay hiding).
- `src/ui/screens/fight.js` needs runtime verification and likely debugging (result stats markup fixed; duplicate `getUp` case fixed; remove of unused helpers done).
- CSS additions still needed for classes from other screens: `create-*`, `alloc-*`, `offer-actions`, `active-contract`, `belts-strip`, `champ-row`, `dossier`, `article-meta/hero`, `news-cat-row`, `drill-grid`, `timing-*`, `training-gain`, `history-row`, `result-badge`, `timeline`, `join-row`, `wager-box`, `chat-panel`, `mp-disclaimer`, responsive rules.
- Visual tuning of boxer poses, arm/guard, KO body offset.
- Verify build and runtime; no tests or README yet.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Finish appending missing CSS rules, especially new fight-screen classes, then run `npm run build` and fix import/runtime errors.
2. Fix any `fight.js` runtime issues found in-browser: result overlay stats/actions, career apply-once, multiplayer state/input sync, pause/replay, touch controls.
3. Verify full menu flow; check settings `data-nav` section buttons cause harmless unknown-screen warnings (consider `data-section`).
4. Run Playwright screenshots (menu/editor/fight/rankings/multiplayer/result) at ≤1280px, save small JPEGs.
5. Add tests (`tests/*.test.mjs`) and README documenting multiplayer/backend assumptions, PeerJS cloud/no TURN limitation, virtual TG COIN, and note assumptions at finish.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/ui/screens/fight.js`: newly created fight screen; main current work item.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/ui/styles.css`: needs new fight CSS appended; existing fight/HUD styles around lines 452–560.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/net/net.js`: PeerJS session; room-ready events now `'room'`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/ui/screens/multiplayer.js`: lobby, handshake, `mpFighterDef`, `getMp`, `sendMp`, `attachMp`, `closeMp`; room event handler renamed.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game/fight.js`: `FightEngine`, `PUNCHES`, snapshots/inputs/events, AI, result.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game/fightview.js`: cinematic view, entrance/replay/belt; `VISUAL_SCALE = 0.68`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/ui/screens/career.js`: navigates `fight` with `{mode:'career', offer, arenaId, rounds, division}`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/core/career.js`: `applyFightResult` consequences/idempotency.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/core/store.js`: save schema, `persist`, `createPlayerFighter`, settings, `addCoins`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/core/data.js`: catalogs, `ARENA_BY_ID`, `DIVISION_BY_ID`, `CONTROL_DEFAULTS`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/ui/icons.js`: inline icon set; `pause` added.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/ui/shell.js`: routing, cleanup lifecycle, toasts/modals.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/app.js`: renderer/background loop, `showFight`, quality.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js`: boot and screen registration.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/ui/helpers.js`: `esc`, `h`, formatting, `screenHead`.

## Important Context
- Game code is new and **uncommitted**; repo originally only had process/runtime scripts and docs.
- Build fails until all imports resolve; `fight.js` now exists, so next check is `npm run build`.
- `FightEngine` starts in `intro`; call `engine.start()` after entrance. Drain `engine.drainEvents()` each frame and pass to `view.handleEvent()` + `audio.handleEvents()`.
- `FightView` constructor: `new FightView({ renderer, engine, arenaConfig, quality, appearances:{p1,p2}, mobile })`; then `ui.app.showFight(view)`.
- Fight screen wraps `view.update` so `tick()` (engine + network + HUD) runs before rendering.
- Host must drive `engine.update(dt,{p1,p2})`; guest must only apply snapshots, send inputs, and not simulate.
- `applyFightResult({ save, universe, result, offer, division, arenaId })`; career p1 is player, `winnerId==='p1'` means win; idempotent via `result.matchId`.
- Multiplayer session in `ui.mp` (`session`, `role`, `match`, `listeners`, `localInfo`, ready/wager state); `ui.mpKeep` prevents lobby cleanup from destroying session when navigating to fight.
- Wager settlement: `save.multiplayer.history` keyed by `match.matchId`, winner +wager, loser −min(wager, coins), receipt via `matchReceipt`.
- PeerJS cloud works for signaling but no TURN server; strict NATs may fail; public rooms limited to `OPEN-0..7`.
- Use `npm run dev` on port 3002 and Playwright headed Chromium/SwiftShader; capture JPEG screenshots ≤1280px.
- `capture.sh` uses runtime default capture; `start.sh` uses runtime default start.
